_comment: Curated import manifest for tools/import_ngcc.py, keyed by the NGCC scheme folder. status: supported (default) | unsupported | skip. tier: board (fits nucleo-l4r5zi) | qemu (mps2-an386 only). copy_dirs are relative to the instance dir ('@path' = relative to schemes/<folder>/). defines -> ngcc_config.h; cflags -> IMPL_CFLAGS_<impl>; exclude_common -> IMPL_EXCLUDE_COMMON_<impl>; sed = [glob, regex, replacement]; patches = repo-relative unified diffs applied with patch -p1 in the impl dir. m4 = submitter-provided Cortex-M4 implementation: {zip_dir: sub-directory of the submission zip (unpacked by tools/extract_ngcc_m4.py into schemes/<folder>/M4_Implementation/), zip_exclude: dir names not to unpack, instances: {<instance>: {dir: path below zip_dir, ...any import rule}}, plus any import rule applying to every m4 instance}; the m4 job inherits the scheme-level rules (except copy_dirs/instances) and the reference instance's defines, and lands in crypto_<fam>/<instance>/m4/. An m4 block with status skip/unsupported documents a submission whose ARM tree is not imported. Hash code: the importer routes every KeccakF1600_StatePermute definition to the assembly permutation in common/keccakf1600.S via KeccakF1600_StatePermute_plain (plain lane state <-> bit-interleaved assembly state) (KECCAK_ASM_SED; opt out with keccak_asm: false); permutations under other names (Lore, NSS-HQC, GreatWall, Lynxer/ReSolveD XKCP) and the schemes' own SM3 compression functions (Phoenix-SM3, Aigis-Sig+, Scloudplus) are routed by per-scheme sed rules to KeccakF1600_StatePermute / sm3_bit_compress(_asm).

PolarLAC._note: Implementations/Reference_Implementation/x86 is portable C (SM3 route, BIT_USE_SHAKE=0); the mirror held the AVX2 Optimized_Implementation/x86 tree until 2026-10-06 (wrong fetch override), which is why this entry used to be 'unsupported'. Official KATs: Test_Vectors/Reference_Implementation/x86 (identical to Optimized/ARM; the Optimized/x86 KATs differ).

m4.reason: Implementations/Optimized_Implementation/ARM is an AArch64 NEON/SVE port (arm_neon.h, vld1q, SVE sampler/FFT helpers), not Cortex-M4 code

Loom.reason: LOOM-AKE is a protocol over Weaver KEM and SHUTTLE signatures (same shape as CreTAKE: per instance kem/, sig/ and a loom/ protocol layer), but it cannot link the implementations in this tree: (1) SHUTTLE is not imported (its Gaussian sampler, irs.c/approx_*.h/sampler_u.c, uses GNU __int128 fixed-point kernels on ~70 lines, unavailable on 32-bit ARM), and Loom's long-term keys and all four passes use SHUTTLE (PKa/PKb are SHUTTLE public keys, 1264 B); (2) Loom's kem/ is a modified Weaver, not the submitted one: crypto_kem_dec is replaced by crypto_kem_dec_rigid with a ciphertext tag (kem_cpaf.c), and cbd.c/msgenc.c differ by hundreds of lines with extra invq tables, so crypto_kem/WeaverKEM-*/ref is not a drop-in dependency. Importable once SHUTTLE has a 32-bit port, with Loom's own kem/ copied as a private dependency.
Loom._note: KAT: Test_Vectors/KAT_KEX_LoomKEX-{128,256,512}.txt; 4 passes, M1 792 B, M2 776 B, M3/M4 1235 B, state 2657 B at level 128.

m4.reason: no Cortex-M4 code in the package

YuanYang.DSA.reason: bigint.c includes <immintrin.h>; double FFT keygen; 709 KB stack frame

CS.reason: does not compile as shipped (missing NTT.h, conflicting static declaration)

NIIKE.reason: isogeny NIKE: 12 MB working set, minutes per run

MAMBA-Frost.reason: Frodo-like matrices: 7.4 MB stack frame (x86 -O3 build)

CreTAKE._note: Protocol-only import: each instance directory holds the CreTAKE protocol layer (KEX_AlgorithmInstance.c, cretake_params.h, primitive_interfaces.h, secure_bzero.c). The KEM/signature backends under Common/primitives are copies of the PolarLAC, ZEN and BiT submissions (K2K first public keys equal the standalone KATs), so the instances link the implementations already in this tree through IMPL_DEPS (see mk/scheme.mk): primitive_interfaces.h's ../../Common/primitives/... includes are rewritten to ../../../crypto_{kem,sign}/<scheme>/ref/. Instances with BiT-256/512 backends are QEMU tier because those BiT sets fault on the board. The 10 component instances in schemes.json (BiT-*, POLARLAC-*, ZEN_*) are benchmarked under their own submissions.

CreTAKE-K2K-PLAC128._note: the K2K-PLAC twopke.c/twokem.c (two-ciphertext KEM) call PolarLAC internals, which must stay exported from the dependency object

BIKE_MLThre.reason: seeds the NIST AES256-CTR DRBG (FromNIST/rng.c, OpenSSL) from the ICCS DRNG; needs a portable CTR-DRBG port

m4.note: pqm4-layout tree; m4fspeed is the only variant shipped per instance (ref/ and m4fstack/ are empty), with its own ICCS glue and SM3 M4 kernels; ntt.c initialises int32_t twiddle tables with 32-bit unsigned bit patterns (intended two's-complement wrap), -Wno-overflow silences the resulting warnings

DTRU._note: official KATs are generated without PK_PACK_OPT (the Makefile's KAT_KEM target)

m4.note: pqm4-layout tree (KEM-DTRU-ARM-Optimized); m4fspeed per instance with Cortex-M4 NTT/basemul assembly and its own ICCS glue; its Test_Vectors/*_SPEED.txt equal the official KAT files (PK_PACK_OPT=0, as for ref) ngccm4 fixes (sed): DTRU-Light's ntt_fast/invntt_fast and DTRU-1024's doublebasemul_asm_opt clobber callee-saved FPU registers (s17/s18, s24) without saving them; vpush/vpop added. The hashing app's main() keeps a zero in d8 (s16/s17), which DTRU-Light overwrote with its Barrett constant 0xffed0ae3.

sed: \1\n  vpush {s24-s25}  @ ngccm4: s24 is callee-saved (AAPCS), the port uses it as scratch\2\n  vpop {s24-s25}\3
